answer: The protocol assigns each new AI agent a reputation token that must be bonded on the wharf of the network’s ledger as a stake. A quadratic weighting function treats the combined stake of n identities as √(∑stake_i) so a single well‑funded agent on the ledge contributes linearly while k Sybil nodes each staking the minimum only add √k·min, drastically reducing their voting power. An attacker therefore must lock up a beacon‑size deposit of 10 ETH per fake identity, making the cost 10 ETH × k and rendering large Sybil farms economically infeasible.
